meta.author: Chat 8A
meta.lineShape: { speaker, text, mood?, choices?[{id,text}] } — exactly what ui/dialogue.js (story:line) renders. speaker ∈ speakers below.
meta.lessonShape: { id, title, lesson, tip } — exactly what ui/ledger.js (story:lesson) renders. id = Economy BALANCE.lessons[season-1].
meta.toastShape: { id, text, icon?, kind?, trigger } — ui/toast.js (story:toast). trigger = bus event name 8B listens to, fired once per run.
meta.ledgerVariants: ledger.low = 0–1 stars · ledger.default = 2 stars · ledger.high = 3 stars (8B picks by report.stars).

pip.name: Pip
pip.role: hero, young Channeler who has never heard a money word in his life (debt? commission? is that a hat?) — innocent, satirical, learns out loud

owl.name: Tally-Owl
owl.role: mentor, keeps the books, dry humour, never scolds twice

baron.name: Baron Gilt
baron.role: villain, Lord of the Debt Fog, pompous, loves asterisks

glimmer.name: Glimmer
glimmer.role: blob customers, speak in short bursts

budgeting.title: Budgeting
budgeting.lesson: A budget is a plan for your Spark before you spend it. Every coin that comes in gets a jar before it gets a wish.
budgeting.tip: Fill the four jars first. Spend only what sits in Spend.

needsVsWants.title: Needs vs Wants
needsVsWants.lesson: Needs keep the market standing: upkeep, repairs, the roof. Wants are lovely, and they can wait one season without anyone getting hurt.
needsVsWants.tip: Ask: if I skip this, does anything break?

emergencyFund.title: Emergency Fund
emergencyFund.lesson: Storms do not send invitations. Spark parked in Protect turns a disaster into a bill — and a bill into a shrug.
emergencyFund.tip: Aim for three seasons of upkeep in Protect.

goodVsBadInterest.title: Good vs Bad Interest
goodVsBadInterest.lesson: Save pays YOU 5 % every season. The Baron charges 20 %, and his interest grows interest of its own. Same word, opposite direction.
goodVsBadInterest.tip: Repay the Baron before you buy anything shiny.

scams.title: Too-Good Deals
scams.lesson: Secret, urgent and guaranteed: if a deal has all three, it is built so you do not think. Real offers survive a night's sleep.
scams.tip: Spot the tells: hurry · secrecy · "guaranteed" · an asterisk.

compoundGrowth.title: Compound Growth
compoundGrowth.lesson: Interest earns interest. A small jar left alone for many seasons quietly becomes a big one — time does the heavy lifting.
compoundGrowth.tip: Start early, even tiny. The calendar is your best helper.

insurance.title: Insurance
insurance.lesson: The Protect jar absorbs shocks so one bad day cannot undo a good season. It feels wasted right up until the moment it isn't.
insurance.tip: Real cover names exactly what it covers and how to claim.

diversification.title: Diversification
diversification.lesson: Spread Spark across stalls and jars. When fish prices dip, the flower stall still hums. Never one stall, never one jar.
diversification.tip: Three kinds of stall beat three of the same.

delayedGratification.title: Delayed Gratification
delayedGratification.lesson: Waiting one season for an upgrade you can afford beats borrowing for it today. Future-Pip is a customer too — treat them well.
delayedGratification.tip: Want it? Price it, save for it, then buy it twice as happily.

planningForAGoal.title: Planning for a Goal
planningForAGoal.lesson: Name the goal, price it, split it into seasons. The Lighthouse was never a dream — it was a plan with a deadline.
planningForAGoal.tip: Goal ÷ seasons left = this season's target. Write it down.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 1 — The Inheritance

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: So this is Glowmarket. My island! My very foggy, very empty island. Is the fog included, or is that extra?

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Welcome, Channeler. My name is Tally-Owl, and I kept your grandmother's books for many years, which means I also kept them honest.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Let me start with the bad news: Glowmarket owes Baron Gilt 260 Spark. That purple haze over the pier is his Debt Fog, and it grows every time we borrow or overspend.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Owes? What is an 'owes'? Is it like a hat? Can I take it off?

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: A debt, Pip. Spark that someone lent us and now wants back, with extra on top. The good news: you have 150 Spark in your pouch, a hammer, and me. Build a stall, sell to the Glimmers, and put every coin you earn into the four jars: Spend, Save, Invest and Protect.

opening.speaker: baron
opening.text: Ahh, the new owner! Baron Gilt, Lord of the Debt Fog, at your service. Do take your time repaying the 260. I charge only 20 %… per season.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Twenty per cent of what? Of me? Tally-Owl, can he take twenty per cent of ME?

opening.speaker: baron
opening.text: Compounding. It is my favourite word. Toodle-oo!

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: We are halfway through the season, so this is a good moment to look at the jars rather than the pile, because a plan for your Spark is worth more than a heap of it.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Fruit! Fruit stall! Shiny!

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Here is your first ledger: income came in, upkeep went out, and a little was left over for the jars. That is all a budget really is, nothing fancier than that.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: So a budget is just telling my coins where to sleep BEFORE they run off. Why does nobody put that on a sign?

low.speaker: owl
low.text: The books are thin this season, but they are open and honest, and nobody budgets perfectly on the first try. The trick is simply to try again next season with what you learned.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: I spent it before the jars. I spent it before the jars. Tally-Owl, is there a jar for lessons? Because I just earned one.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Three stars on your very first ledger. I believe your grandmother would have made a rather undignified hooting noise at this.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: Three stars! For doing the thing you told me to do! Being a grown-up is suspiciously easy. What's the catch?

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 2 — Needs and Wants

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Tally-Owl! The Tool Smith has a GOLDEN awning. I need one. For the fruit. Fruit loves gold, probably.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Now imagine the fruit stall with a roof that does not leak, and ask yourself which of the two actually keeps the Glimmers coming back.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: …the roof. Fine. The roof. The fruit will just have to be rained on in a NON-golden way.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Needs come first, and that means upkeep, repairs and the walk to the pier. Wants can wait one season, because unlike fruit they do not spoil.

opening.speaker: collector
opening.text: Levy notice! The Baron reminds you his interest is growing nicely. Have a dreadful day!

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Here is a quick test you can apply to every purchase: if you skip it, does anything break? If nothing breaks, then it is a want rather than a need.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Too pricey. Hmph.

default.speaker: owl
default.text: You paid every need, bought a want or two, and the Fog held still, which makes this a thoroughly sensible season.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: So a 'need' is a thing that breaks, and a 'want' is a thing that sparkles. I've been shopping with the wrong eyeballs.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: The Fog grew this season, which usually means a want jumped the queue in front of a need somewhere. It happens to everyone, and now you know exactly what it costs.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: The want cut in line in front of the need. It had a ribbon on. Ribbons are how they get you.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Every need was covered, the Fog was pushed back, and you still had Spark left over for Save. That is how a market grows old gracefully.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: The roof doesn't leak and I FEEL things about it. Is this what being sensible is like? It's weirdly fizzy.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 3 — The Storm Season

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: There are grey clouds gathering over the Far Point, and Spark Storms tend to arrive at this time of year without sending an invitation first.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: An invitation? Storms are supposed to send invitations?! That's the most polite thing I've heard about weather.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: They break things, and broken things cost Spark. If that Spark is already sitting in Protect, a storm is just a bill; if it is not, the wind scatters a tenth of whatever sits in Save and Invest, and what is still owed becomes a loan — and the lender will be him.

opening.speaker: baron
opening.text: Did somebody say loan? Terrible weather we are having. Wonderful weather for lending!

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: So the Protect jar is a bodyguard for my other jars. A jar bodyguard. I'll fill it before the sky gets rude.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: The Protect jar may look idle, but that is entirely the point, because it is the one jar that works hardest on your worst day.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Wind! Hold my hat!

default.speaker: owl
default.text: The storm came, Protect paid for the damage, and the Baron went home hungry, which is precisely what an emergency fund is for.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: The storm came, and all that happened was a bill. A BILL. I've never been so happy to be charged for something.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: The storm hit an empty Protect jar, so the Fog rolled in to fill the gap. I would refill it before the next one arrives.

low.speaker: baron
low.text: Lovely doing business, as always.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Protect was full, the storm barely registered, and the Fog actually shrank. Your grandmother used to call seasons like this boring, and I have always found boring rather beautiful.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: The storm hit and nothing moved. Nothing! Boring is beautiful. Put it on the awning. The non-golden awning.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 4 — Two Kinds of Interest

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Tally-Owl, the Save jar grew overnight. By ITSELF. Is it alive? Should I feed it? Does it bite?

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: It is working as intended: Save pays you 5 % every season, and that is what good interest looks like, Spark that keeps working while you sleep.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: The Baron's loan is the same word pointing the other way, 20 % a season growing on top of itself. Bad interest also works while you sleep, except that it works against you.

opening.speaker: baron
opening.text: Pointing the other way! How poetic. Shall I round your balance UP for you? No charge. Well — one small charge.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Wait, so my jar has the nice kind of interest and the Baron has the evil twin? Repay the evil twin first. Got it.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Every coin you repay is a coin the Baron can never charge interest on again, which makes repayment the best return available anywhere on this island.

mid.speaker: collector
mid.text: Balance reminder! It went up! Isn't that nice? For us.

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Interest earned sits on one line and interest paid on the other. If you make the first number bigger than the second every season, the Fog simply has nowhere left to grow.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: One interest grows my pile, the other grows his. Same word. Somebody should've invented two words.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: This season the Baron earned more from you than Save earned for you. Let us flip that next season by repaying before you spend.

low.speaker: baron
low.text: Compounding! Still my favourite word.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Debt went down, Save went up, and the gap between them is exactly where the Fog used to live. That earns you three stars.

high.speaker: baron
high.text: You repaid EARLY? That is simply rude.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 5 — Too-Good Deals

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: The Baron has grown bored of waiting, so expect visitors bearing wonderful offers. I should mention that 'wonderful offer' is his second favourite phrase.

opening.speaker: collector
opening.text: Psst. Exclusive deal. Today only. Guaranteed. Don't tell the owl.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Secret, urgent AND guaranteed? That sounds wonderful. Tally-Owl, why is your face doing that thing?

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Precisely. A genuine offer survives a night's sleep, whereas a Too-Good Deal cannot, because it depends on you deciding before you have had time to think.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Look for the tells: a sense of hurry, a request for secrecy, the word 'guaranteed', and his personal favourite, a very tiny asterisk.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Nobody can guarantee growth, and anyone who claims to is not really selling growth at all. What they are selling is you.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: A collector tried to sell me a lantern that 'might' be lucky. I kept my coins.

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Offers came and went, and the jars are exactly where you left them. Saying no remains the cheapest financial tool ever invented.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: Secret, urgent, guaranteed: the three magic words that mean 'run'. I also learned what an asterisk is. It's a tiny star that eats money.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: A deal that looked too good turned out to be exactly as good as it looked. It was an expensive lesson, but it is far cheaper to learn it now than later.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: I didn't read the asterisk. I didn't know asterisks were READABLE. Next time I sleep on it. On the deal. Physically.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: You refused every Too-Good Deal and spotted every tell, and I notice the Collectors have started avoiding your pier altogether.

high.speaker: baron
high.text: Who TAUGHT you about asterisks?!

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 6 — The Quiet Jar

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Tally-Owl, I did the sums. Twice, because the first time I didn't believe me. Save earned MORE this season and I didn't add a single coin. Is the jar cheating?

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Your interest has started earning interest of its own, so the jar is now paying you on the Spark it already paid you earlier. That is compounding, and this is the good kind.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Start small, start early, and leave it alone. Those three habits have built more lighthouses than any treasure chest ever did.

opening.speaker: baron
opening.text: Compounding is MY word. Give it back.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: You can't own a word, Baron. I checked. Well, I asked an owl. Same thing.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Invest grows faster than Save, but it wobbles along the way, while Save is the steady tortoise. The island has room for both of them.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Your market got bigger! Or did I get smaller?

default.speaker: owl
default.text: That is growth on top of growth. The calendar did half of this season's work for you, and the calendar never asks for upkeep.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: Interest earning interest earning interest. It's coins having coin babies. I'm leaving them alone to do their thing.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: An emptied Save jar cannot compound, because every withdrawal resets all of its quiet work. Try to let it sit untouched next season.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: I keep opening the quiet jar to see if it's working. Apparently that's how you stop it working. Jars are shy.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Save, Invest and the stalls all grew on top of last season's growth, which makes this the season the island started paying for itself.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: The quiet jar is the LOUD jar now! I did nothing and it's my best employee!

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 7 — Cover

opening.speaker: collector
opening.text: Introducing Fog-Proof Insurance™! Covers everything*! No paperwork! *Terms do not exist.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Real cover tells you exactly what it covers and exactly how you make a claim. If there are no terms, then there is no cover, only a fee.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Insurance? Is that a spell? Can I buy it from the Tool Smith? Does it come with a ribbon?

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: That would be the Protect jar. It absorbs storms, leaky roofs and Collector 'levies' so that one bad day cannot undo a good season, and the Guard Tortoise helps it absorb even more.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: So real cover names what it covers and how to claim. And the Baron's version names a price and an asterisk. I'm learning to count asterisks now. It's a skill.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Insurance feels wasted in every season where nothing happens, but that feeling is simply the price of being covered, and it is still far cheaper than the Fog.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: A roof! It kept the rain off my purchase!

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Shocks came, Protect absorbed them, and the season stayed whole. Good cover does its best work when nobody notices it at all.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: One bad day, zero bad seasons. The Protect jar didn't do anything until it did EVERYTHING.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: Protect ran dry and the Fog filled the gap. I would top it up before chasing another stall, with defence coming first this time.

low.speaker: collector
low.text: Our policy would not have helped either, honestly.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: You are fully covered and the Fog has pulled back to the pier, leaving the Collectors standing in a very small puddle of purple.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: Boring is beautiful, part two. I'm starting to think boring is my favourite colour.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 8 — Many Baskets

opening.speaker: glimmer
opening.text: Fish is cheap this season! Everyone has fish! Too much fish!

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: If my whole market were fish stalls I'd be in trouble right now. So THAT'S why you keep saying 'spread'. I thought it was a bread thing.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: That is diversification in a single sentence: different stalls, different jars and different Glimmers, so that when one of them dips, the others carry you through.

opening.speaker: baron
opening.text: I have a hot tip. Put EVERYTHING in Quick-Flip Spark Notes. I personally know the fellow who prints them.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: 'I personally know' is not a plan, Baron, it is a tell, and I have heard that particular one many times before.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Three different kinds of stall will always beat three of the same. The West Meadow and the East Shore are not just extra land, they are different baskets for your eggs.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Tea AND flowers AND fish? I need a bigger bag.

default.speaker: owl
default.text: One trade dipped while two others hummed along, and the season balanced itself out. Spreading your risk is the quietest kind of safety there is.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: Never one stall, never one jar. Never one anything, really. Except one Baron. One is already plenty.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: You had too many eggs in one stall this season, and the dip found every one of them. I would open a different trade before adding a third of the same kind.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: I really do love fish though. Can diversifying be eight fish stalls that are slightly different colours? No? Noted.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Every zone is trading, every jar is working, and the dip barely left a mark. This island has become a very hard thing to knock over.

high.speaker: baron
high.text: Nobody bought my Spark Notes. NOBODY.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 9 — The Long Wait

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: The Far Point is ALMOST affordable. Almost! Baron, if I borrowed just a tiny— why is everyone looking at me like that?

opening.speaker: baron
opening.text: Say no more! Pre-approved! Ink still wet!

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Pip, one more season of saving buys the Far Point outright. Borrowing would buy it today, but then you would keep paying for it every season afterwards.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: …Future-Pip is a customer too. And Future-Pip would be furious. Future-Pip sounds exhausting. I'll wait.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Treat your wants well: decide you want it, price it, save for it, and then buy it twice as happily.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Waiting is not the same as doing nothing, because every day you wait, Save and Invest are quietly doing the work for you.

mid.speaker: collector
mid.text: Last chance to borrow! (It is not the last chance. It is never the last chance.)

default.speaker: owl
default.text: On a ledger, patience looks like one boring season followed by a wonderful one, and you are now halfway to wonderful.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: One more season. I can wait one more season. I have waited for soup to cool. This is basically soup.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: Something was bought early with borrowed Spark, and the Fog thanked you for it. Next season, I suggest we let the want wait.

low.speaker: baron
low.text: Pre-approved and PROUD of it.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Not a single coin borrowed, the Far Point funded in full, and the Fog has nothing left to feed on. There is just one season to go.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: Future-Pip says thank you. Loudly. Future-Pip is here now, by the way. It's me. I'm Future-Pip. It's great.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 10 — The Lighthouse

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Ten seasons ago the goal was a single sentence: relight the Lighthouse. Then we priced it, split it into seasons, and hit the targets one by one.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Goal divided by seasons left equals this season's target. I wrote it on the fruit stall. The Glimmers think it's a price. Nobody has paid it yet.

opening.speaker: baron
opening.text: You cannot relight it. The Fog is MINE. I have asterisks on it!

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: The Fog is a debt, Baron, and debts tend to go very quiet once they have been paid.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Last season. Ten seasons ago I didn't know what a debt was. Now I have a plan with a DEADLINE. Who am I?

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: This is the final stretch, with Protect full, debt at zero and every jar doing its job. Walk to the Far Point as soon as the Fog lifts.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Is that… light? On the hill? LIGHT!

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Ten ledgers, ten lessons, and one plan with a deadline that you actually kept, so I think it is time you looked up, Pip.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: The Lighthouse… I planned this. Me. A person who thought 'owes' was a hat.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: The last season wobbled a little, but the plan held. A goal does not need a perfect final step, it only needs a final step.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: We made it. Barely! Barely is a kind of made it. Barely still gets the lighthouse.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: That is a perfect final ledger. Your grandmother's books never looked this good, and I say that as the owl who kept them.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: Every jar full, every lesson learned, every asterisk read. Light it up before I cry on the ledger!

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Exclusive! A Zero-Interest* Loan of 150 Spark. Zero! Today only, don't tell the owl.

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Signed! Zero interest for exactly one season, then 35 % per season. Compounding. Toodle-oo!

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: It was the asterisk, Pip, and in my experience it is always the asterisk that costs you.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: The asterisk? Oh, it's tiny. Barely a footnote. 35 % after the first season. Compounding. Why do you ask?

refuse.speaker: pip
refuse.text: Thirty-five per cent is NOT zero. I may be new, but I can count to zero. No thank you. Loudly.

zeroInterestLoan.tell: The asterisk. *Zero for one season, then 35 % per season — compounding.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Hand me 80 Spark and I will hand you 160 back next season. Guaranteed! The Baron himself guarantees it!

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Marvellous! Your Spark is now on its way to… somewhere. Guaranteed to be somewhere!

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: Nobody can guarantee growth, Pip. Anyone who claims to is selling something else entirely, and in this case the something else was you.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: Who guarantees the— look, it's guaranteed, that's what the word is FOR.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: Guaranteed returns do not exist, so that was a very good instinct.

doubleSpark.tell: "Guaranteed" returns do not exist. Anyone who guarantees growth is selling something else.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Lucky Lantern Raffle! 40 Spark a ticket, the prize is inside the box, and the box closes in TEN SECONDS!

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Sold! And the prize is… a very nice feeling. Congratulations!

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: Urgency combined with a prize you cannot inspect is a classic pairing. If you must act right now, the deal has been built so that you do not have time to think.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: Open it FIRST? That's— that's not how a raffle— seven! Six!

refuse.speaker: pip
refuse.text: Take your time counting. I'll be over here, keeping my Spark and not winning a feeling.

luckyLantern.tell: Urgency + a prize you cannot inspect. If you must act NOW, the deal is built for you to not think.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Fog-Proof Insurance! 60 Spark, covers everything, no forms, no fuss, no written anything!

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Sign here. Well, there's no 'here'. Just nod.

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Nodded! You are now fully insured against things we will decide later!

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: There were no written terms and no claims process. Real insurance names exactly what it covers and how to claim, which is exactly what the Protect jar does.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: Exactly? It covers… fog-related… circumstances. Broadly. In spirit.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: A policy with no terms is just a fee wearing a hat, so that was well refused.

foggyInsurance.tell: No written terms, no claims process. Real insurance names exactly what it covers and how to claim.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Premium Stall Kit! Normally 300 Spark, today just 120! The Tool Smith would NEVER match that.

choices.text: What does the Tool Smith actually charge?

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Wrapped! It's a hammer. A regular hammer. The premium part is the ribbon.

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: A fake 'normal' price makes a bad price look like a gift. For the record, the Tool Smith's level-2 upgrade costs 90.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: The Tool Smith? Ninety. But OURS has a ribbon.

refuse.speaker: pip
refuse.text: I'll take the 90 without the ribbon, thanks. Ribbons were how they got me last time. I've grown.

premiumStallKit.tell: A fake "normal" price. Compare against what the Tool Smith actually charges (L2 = 90).

pitch.speaker: baron
pitch.text: Pip, between us: Quick-Flip Spark Notes. 100 in, triple out. I personally know the printer.

choices.text: A tip from a stranger is not a plan

accept.speaker: baron
accept.text: Splendid! The printer sends his regards and about thirty Spark. Markets, eh?

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: 'I personally know' is not a plan, and insider tips from strangers are the oldest Too-Good Deal on the sea.

refuse.speaker: baron
refuse.text: A STRANGER? I am a Baron!

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: Spreading your Spark rather than flipping it is exactly the right instinct, and that was very well said.

quickFlip.tell: "I personally know" is not a plan. Insider tips from strangers are the oldest Too-Good Deal.

storm.speaker: owl
storm.text: There is a Spark Storm over the stalls. If Protect is full, this is only a bill; if it is not, brace yourself — the wind does not spare Save and Invest.

festival.speaker: owl
festival.text: A windfall is a test rather than a reward, so put it in a jar before you spend any of it.

collectorVisit.speaker: collector
collectorVisit.text: Routine levy! Nothing personal. Entirely personal.

sparkDip.speaker: owl
sparkDip.text: That was a Spark Dip, and Invest wobbled downwards. This is exactly why Invest is one jar out of four rather than all four.

sparkBoom.speaker: owl
sparkBoom.text: A Spark Boom has sent Invest jumping upwards. Enjoy it, but remember that it wobbles in both directions.

leakyRoof.speaker: pip
leakyRoof.text: The roof! Water on the fruit! Is this a need or a want?! It feels like a NEED!

leakyRoof.speaker: owl
leakyRoof.text: That is a need, not a want, and Protect will cover it.

touristBoat.speaker: glimmer
touristBoat.text: Tourists! We have no idea what anything costs!

baronTax.speaker: baron
baronTax.text: A small Fog Levy. For the upkeep of the Fog. You understand.

baronTax.speaker: owl
baronTax.text: That, Pip, is simply bad interest wearing a hat and hoping nobody notices.

helperDay.speaker: owl
helperDay.text: It is Helper Appreciation Day. Upkeep is a need, and so is saying thank you to the people who earn it.

lighthouseFlicker.speaker: pip
lighthouseFlicker.text: Did the Lighthouse just wink at me? Tally-Owl, can buildings flirt?

lighthouseFlicker.speaker: owl
lighthouseFlicker.text: The Lighthouse remembers you, and every honest ledger brings it a little closer to lighting, so keep going.

win.speaker: pip
win.text: The Fog is… gone. It's just gone. Where does a fog GO? Does it have a home? Does it owe someone?

win.speaker: baron
win.text: Impossible! Nobody repays! Nobody budgets! Nobody READS THE ASTERISK!

win.speaker: owl
win.text: A debt that is fully paid goes quiet, Baron. Perhaps you should try saving instead: five percent every season, and it compounds, which I hear is your favourite word.

win.speaker: collector
win.text: Does this mean we can stop collecting? We'd quite like a stall. A tea stall.

win.speaker: pip
win.text: Channel it, Tally-Owl! Everything we saved — into the Lighthouse! And then explain the word 'channel', I've been nodding for ten seasons.

win.speaker: owl
win.text: Ten seasons, ten lessons, and one plan with a deadline that held together to the end. Go and light it up, Channeler.

win.speaker: narrator
win.text: The Lighthouse of Glowmarket is lit.

endlessUnlock.speaker: owl
endlessUnlock.text: The story ends here, but a market never really does. Endless mode is now open, with no Baron and no deadline, just the island and your jars.

endlessUnlock.speaker: pip
endlessUnlock.text: No Baron, no deadline, just jars. Let's see how big Glowmarket can glow. And how many fish stalls count as 'spread'.

lose.speaker: baron
lose.text: The Fog has the island. Nothing personal — compounding is simply very good at its job.

lose.speaker: owl
lose.text: Every ledger you wrote is still in the books, Pip, and the island remembers its lessons even when the Fog wins.

lose.speaker: pip
lose.text: Next time: jars first, repay early, read the asterisk. I know the words now. I just need to do them in that order.

tutorial.text: Drag the left side (or WASD) to walk. Pip is small; the island is not.
Press B (or the 🔨 button) to build your first stall near the pier. Glimmers arrive there.
Stall placed! Glimmers walk to it, browse, and pay Spark. Fair prices make happy blobs.
First sale! Every coin lands in your pouch — that is your Spend jar. Press APPLY on the jars to split it into Save, Invest and Protect.
Jars set. Save pays 5 %/season, Invest wobbles 8±4 %, Protect absorbs shocks, Spend buys things.
The purple bar is Debt Fog. Borrowing and overspending grow it. Repaying and Protect shrink it.
A Collector has an offer. Secret + urgent + guaranteed = a Too-Good Deal. Look for the tell.
Events happen every season. A full Protect jar turns most of them into a shrug.
Season over! The Ledger shows income, interest earned, interest paid, and your stars. Read the lesson card.
Upgraded! Level 2 sells +50 %, Level 3 +120 % — but upkeep rises too. Needs vs wants.
